Plot the FDP+ Diagnostic Curve

Source: R/visualization.R
plot_fdr_graph.Rd

Displays how the FDP+ diagnostic (a decoy-based estimate of the false discovery proportion under the STABL procedure) changes across the full range of candidate stability thresholds, and marks the threshold selected by the first-minimum rule.

Usage

plot_fdr_graph(object, title = "FDP+ diagnostic", reference_fdp_plus = 0.05)

Arguments

object

A fitted "stabl_fit" object returned by stabl_fit().

title

Character scalar; plot title. Default "FDP+ diagnostic".

reference_fdp_plus

Numeric scalar or NULL; a purely visual horizontal reference line only. It is not used for fitting or threshold selection and marks no control guarantee. Use NULL to omit the line. Default 0.05. (Renamed from fdr_target in 1.0.0: the line is a visual reference, not an FDR-control target.)

Value

A ggplot object. The curve shows the FDP+ diagnostic at each candidate threshold; a vertical dashed line marks the selected threshold stored in object$fdr_min_threshold_; a horizontal dashed line marks reference_fdp_plus when supplied.

Details

This diagnostic shows why a particular stability threshold was chosen during fitting: the current rule selects the first minimum of the displayed FDP+ curve. Curve shape is descriptive and does not by itself establish FDP control, calibration, or signal/noise separation; the minimized value is a data-dependent diagnostic, not a controlled or nominal FDR. Interpretation depends on the artificial-feature assumptions and the fitted data.

Requires that object was fitted with artificial_type set (not NULL).

See also

stabl_fit(), plot_stabl_path()

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1L)
  x <- matrix(rnorm(60 * 8), 60, 8,
               dimnames = list(paste0("s", 1:60), paste0("f", 1:8)))
  y <- setNames(rnorm(60), rownames(x))
  fit <- stabl_fit(x, y,
                   lambda_grid        = data.frame(lambda = c(0.3, 0.1, 0.05)),
                   n_bootstraps       = 6L,
                   hard_threshold     = NULL,
                   artificial_type    = "random_permutation",
                   random_state       = 1L)
  plot_fdr_graph(fit)
}

# }
